title: 2018 FIFA World Cup
summary:
This document is a comprehensive Wikipedia-style article about the 2018 FIFA World Cup, the 21st edition of the quadrennial international football championship, held in Russia from 14 June to 15 July 2018. The article covers the tournament's key facts, including that France defeated Croatia 4–2 in the final at Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow to claim their second title, with individual honors going to Luka Modrić (Golden Ball), Harry Kane (Golden Boot), Thibaut Courtois (Golden Glove), and Kylian Mbappé (Best Young Player).

The document is organized into several major sections: **Host selection**, detailing the bidding process, Russia's victory in the December 2010 vote, and extensive criticism surrounding the decision—including concerns about racism, human rights abuses, migrant laborer mistreatment, and corruption allegations involving FIFA officials and the bidding process. The **Teams** section describes the qualification process (with all 209 FIFA member associations entering for the first time, and Iceland and Panama making their debuts) and the December 2017 group stage draw. The **Squads** and **Officiating** sections cover squad regulations and the historic introduction of video assistant referees (VAR) for the first time in a World Cup.

The article extensively details the **Venues**—twelve stadiums across eleven cities (nine newly built, three renovated)—along with **preparation and costs**, noting the record $14.2 billion price tag, infrastructure investments, volunteer programs, and transportation arrangements. Match-related sections cover the **opening ceremony**, the **group stage** (highlighting defending champions Germany's historic first-round elimination and Japan's advancement via fair play criteria), the **knockout stage**, and **statistics** including goalscorers and discipline records.

Additional sections address **Awards** (including the Dream Team, All-Star Team, and prize money), **Marketing** (branding, broadcasting rights including 4K production, ticketing with the Fan-ID visa-free system, and merchandise), and **Symbols** (the wolf mascot Zabivaka, the Telstar 18 match ball, and official music). The document also covers **Controversies** such as doping allegations, sex trafficking concerns, and diplomatic tensions following the Skripal poisoning, alongside **critical reception** that widely praised Russia's hosting, record global **audience** figures of 3.572 billion viewers, and tournament **sponsorship** details.
